claim: The Recognition hint that separates this まえ from 'before' and 'in front of' does it by printing the English answer, so the front asks nothing.
evidence: Recognition front: 'まえ / after a length of time, as in 300 years ago'. Answer: '…ago'.
fix: Keep the disambiguation but in Japanese: 'after a length of time, as in 300ねんまえ' (or みっかまえ, which the note already uses), so the learner still has to supply 'ago'.
verdictReason: The cue is the card's `scene` field (cards.json), which renders on the Recognition FRONT before the answer, and it contains the answer word 'ago' verbatim; card-authoring-rules.md: 'a scene must never contain or paraphrase the answer'. Note for the fixer: quoted Japanese in a scene normally needs romaji plus a gloss, but the rules exempt a gloss that would give the answer away, so '300ねんまえ (sanbyaku-nen mae)' with no English gloss is the compliant form.

claim: The hint opens with the word 'after' on a card for まえ, which I learned as 'before' while あと is 'after', so on first read it points the wrong way.
evidence: Hint on both faces: 'after a length of time, as in 300 years ago'. Earlier cards: まえ | Before (Lesson 17); あと | After (Lesson 18).
fix: Say where the word goes rather than using 'after': for example 'placed right behind a length of time (number + counter)'.
verdictReason: The ledger confirms まえ | Before (Lesson 17) and あと | After (Lesson 18), and the scene does open with 'after'. But the wording is accurate (まえ sits after the duration) and the deck's own Lesson 17 note already uses 'after' positionally ('まえ after a verb means before'), so whether a learner misreads it is judgement. Settled in practice by the rewrite for chapter-22/mae-ago/leaks-answer/1, which touches the same line; the fixer should word that rewrite without a leading 'after'.

claim: The note cites a book mark I have never seen and a term ('ru-verb') no card has taught, where every other note says Regular 2.
evidence: Note: 'Marked (R2) in the book: a ru-verb (Regular II).'
fix: Say it the way the deck's other notes do: 'A Regular 2 verb: いれます → いれる → いれない.'
verdictReason: Rendered note is exactly as quoted. 'ru-verb' appears nowhere in the ledger (3,154 earlier cards). The book's VOCABULARY line does print 'いれます (R2)', so the mark is faithful, but 'Marked ... in the book' is a book citation on a learner-facing note and teaches nothing the learner can use; the deck's convention is 'Regular 1/2' (ledger: 65 + 45 uses against 3 'Regular II').

claim: This lesson names the verb groups two ways: Roman numerals on the ない-form notes and Arabic numerals on the dictionary-form notes, though Lesson 15 taught them as Regular 1 and Regular 2.
evidence: nai-kawanai: 'a Regular I verb'; nai-minai: 'Regular II'; iremasu-put-in: 'Regular II'; tatsu-dict-form: 'Regular 1'; ireru-dict-form: 'Regular 2'; travel-dont-forget (extras): 'a Regular II verb'.
fix: Use one spelling, Regular 1 / Regular 2 as Lesson 15 does, on every note.
verdictReason: Rendered shipping notes in chapter-22 carry both spellings: 'Regular I/II' on toranaide-kudasai, irenaide-kudasai, iremasu-put-in and all the nai-* cards, 'Regular 1/2' on the *-dict-form cards; chapter-22-extras/travel-dont-forget says 'Regular II'. The ledger's convention is Arabic (Regular 1 x65, Regular 2 x45, Regular II x3) and the book's own GRAMMAR 1 in this chapter writes 'Regular 1 verbs' / 'Regular 2 verbs', so Arabic is the spelling to standardise on.

claim: The sentence needs はこ (box), which no earlier card teaches, and unlike こおり and まだ in this same unit it gets no note.
evidence: Production front: 'Please don't put the pen in the box.' Answer: 'はこのなかにペンをいれないでください'. No はこ / 'Box' line in the ledger; card has no note.
fix: Add a note 'はこ means box', as travel-no-ice does for こおり, or use a container already taught (e.g. かばん or ひきだし).
verdictReason: The ledger does teach it: 'はこ | Box' is a card in chapter-12-extras (Lesson 12: Asking about Places, Extras), ledger line 1902. The Learner's grep missed it. The word is taught, so no note is owed.

claim: 'Please don't worry.' wants しんぱいしないでください, but the same English 'please don't worry' is きにしないでください on another card, and 'Please don't worry about it.' is too, so on Production I cannot tell which verb is wanted.
evidence: travel-dont-worry Production front: 'Please don't worry.' -> しんぱいしないでください. ki-ni-suru-no-wa-yokunai: '...so please don't worry.' -> ...きにしないでください. ki-ni-shinaide-kudasai: 'Please don't worry about it.' -> きにしないでください.
fix: Put a hint on travel-dont-worry naming the word ('with しんぱい'), or give it a different English such as 'Please don't be anxious.'
verdictReason: Verified on the rendered faces: travel-dont-worry ('Please don't worry.') and chapter-22/ki-ni-shinaide-kudasai ('Please don't worry about it.') are both in Emotions & Feelings, neither carries a hint or scene, and 'about it' is the only difference. The base card teaches きにします as 'Worry about', so a learner will reach for きにしないでください on either front. Preflight's collision check passes because the normalized glosses are not byte-identical, so nothing else reports it. The note on travel-dont-worry explains the difference, but only on the back. ki-ni-suru-no-wa-yokunai is less affected since its first half names the structure.

claim: This front and the base card's front differ only by square brackets, so in a shuffle I will often give one answer to the other.
evidence: please-dont-photo Production: 'Please don't take photos.' -> しゃしんをとらないでください. toranaide-kudasai (chapter-22) Production: 'Please don't take [photos].' -> とらないでください.
fix: Hint the base card ('the verb alone, no object') or rewrite its English as 'Please don't take (it).'
verdictReason: Facts check out: the two Production fronts differ only by the brackets and the category label (Other vs Grammar & Function Words), and neither card carries a hint. The brackets are the book's own gloss ('please don't take [photos]'), which the parenthetical convention keeps in `english`, and the deck uses them throughout for an object the target omits, so a learner who has absorbed that convention is cued. please-dont-photo was shipped despite its own reviewNote flagging it as 'possibly already taught'. Whether brackets alone are enough cue is judgement; a hint on the base card settles it cheaply.

claim: The English says 'sake' for おさけ, but the base card's note told me おさけ is alcohol in general and bare さけ is the rice wine, so 'sake' points me to the wrong form. A sister card translates the same おさけ as 'alcohol'.
evidence: osake-ex1: 'I drink sake with a friend.' -> ともだちとおさけをのみます. osake note: 'The お is optional, and is usual when talking about alcohol in general. Without it, さけ often means Japanese rice wine in particular.' nai-nomanai-ex1: 'Please don't drink alcohol today.' -> ...おさけを...
fix: Change the English to 'I drink (alcohol) with a friend.' to match nai-nomanai-ex1.
verdictReason: The book glosses the headword as '(お)さけ alcoholic drink, sake', so 'sake' for おさけ is a faithful gloss and the card is not wrong. The expectation that 'sake' implies bare さけ comes entirely from the base card's note, which the Reader separately shows is a distinction the book does not make (chapter-22/osake/note-unverifiable/1). Fix the note and this card needs no change.

claim: Three notes are written for the deck's builders, not for me: they cite book exercises I do not have or describe the card's own category, and teach nothing.
evidence: sawarimasu-touch-ex1: 'Reuses the book's own Exercise 2 stimulus sentence (item 4, before its transformation into the ないでください drill).' nai-nomanai-ex1: 'Reuses the chapter's own Speaking Practice line (the doctor's instruction).' nai-kawanai-ex1: 'An inflected ない-form, not a function word: one sentence, delivered inside this chapter's verb[ない-form]でください pattern rather than as a bare plain-form ending.'
fix: Delete these notes, or move them to reviewNote; for nai-nomanai-ex1, the doctor setting would work as a scene ('A doctor to a patient').
verdictReason: All three strings sit in the learner-facing `note` field in chapter-22-extras/cards.json and render on both faces exactly as quoted. They are authoring rationale (provenance and category justification), which card-authoring-rules.md assigns to `reviewNote`, 'shown ONLY at the review gate, NEVER in the deck'. None adds anything the learner can use.

claim: The book's register note for verb ないでください (a fairly strong instruction, softened by giving a reason) is on no card, and this card's note presents the request as simply polite.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 2: "This is a fairly strong expression which is used by managers or officials when giving instructions to people. When wishing to soften the expression, in most cases it is used along with some reason the action should not be taken (KS1)." Card note: "The ない-form inside is casual, but ください makes the whole request polite." No note in chapter-22 or chapter-22-extras mentions strength or softening.
fix: Add to the toranaide-kudasai note that ないでください is a fairly firm instruction and that giving a reason first (〜ですから、〜ないでください, as in KS1) softens it.
verdictReason: Book GRAMMAR 2 (chapter 48 outline) says exactly this. A grep of both units' cards.json for strong/soften/firm/reason finds only two reviewer flags, no note. The ですから reason-first shape is demonstrated by several extras sentences (nai-kawanai-ex1, no-parking-sign, dangerous-dont-stand) but never explained, and the toranaide-kudasai note's 'ください makes the whole request polite' leaves the learner thinking it is an ordinary polite request. should-fix stands: the omission changes how the learner would use the form.

claim: The note claims that さけ without お often means rice wine in particular, a distinction the book does not make and which does not hold reliably.
evidence: Book, VOCABULARY: "( お ) さけ alcoholic drink, sake". Card note: "The お is optional, and is usual when talking about alcohol in general. Without it, さけ often means Japanese rice wine in particular."
fix: Say instead that お is the polite prefix (as in おすし) and that both forms mean alcohol in general or sake.
verdictReason: The book's only statement is the headword '(お)さけ alcoholic drink, sake', with no sense split between the prefixed and bare forms; the deck's rule treats a bracketed optional part as one entry, not two senses. The ledger already carries にほんしゅ | Sake (Japanese rice liquor) for the rice-wine sense, so the note introduces a distinction the deck handles elsewhere and the learner cannot check. Fixing this note also removes the cause of the rejected chapter-22-extras/osake-ex1/other/1.
